title: Small-Angle Approximation sin x approx x in Radian Mode vs. Degree Mode
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: When x is measured in radians, \sin x \approx x for numerically small values of x (with error less than 1 in 5000 for |x| < 0.1). (a) Graph y = \sin x and y = x together in radian mode near the origin and describe what happens as x approaches 0. (b) Graph y = \sin x and y = x together in degree mode near the origin and explain why the picture differs from radian mode.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } y = \sin x \text{ and } y = x \text{ coalesce with slope } 1 \text{ at } x = 0; \quad \text{(b) in degrees, } \sin(x^\circ) = \sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right) \approx \frac{\pi}{180}x \text{ has slope } \frac{\pi}{180} \approx 0.0175 \ne 1

steps.title: Analyze Part (a): Behavior Near the Origin in Radian Mode
steps.explanation: In radian mode, as x approaches 0, the curve y = sin x and the line y = x become visually indistinguishable because y = x is the tangent line to y = sin x at (0, 0) with slope 1.
steps.why: On a unit circle, the chord/height sin x and the arc length x have ratio approaching 1 as the radian angle x approaches 0.

steps.title: Analyze Part (b): Analytical Formula of Sine in Degree Mode
steps.explanation: When a grapher is set to degree mode, an input x is interpreted as x degrees, which equals pi*x/180 radians.
steps.why: Converting x degrees to radians multiplies x by pi/180.

steps.title: Compare the Slopes Near the Origin in Degree Mode
steps.explanation: Near the origin in degree mode, y = sin(x^circ) behaves like a very flat line of slope pi/180 approx 0.01745, whereas y = x has slope 1. Thus the two graphs cross at a sharp angle at (0, 0) rather than merging.
steps.why: Scaling the horizontal axis by 180/pi compresses the slope of the sine curve by pi/180.
